1.why: UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with clear letter spacing and comfortable line spacing across all screens.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case with no italics, all-caps, or dense text blocks.

3.why: Content is in a narrow centered card with large controls and spacing that fits a mobile viewport.

4.why: Copy is short and plain, e.g. “Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone.”

5.why: Phone field shows an example placeholder (+447700900000), but email and code fields give no input example.

6.why: User only ever sees brief one- or two-sentence instructions before acting.

7.why: No copy control or equivalent is shown for the verification code; it must be typed manually.

8.why: No QR code or alternative to manual code entry appears on any screen.

9.why: Screens show plain inputs only; no evidence of autofill, one-time-code, or password-manager support.

10.why: “Step X of 3” label and the solid primary button make the current step and main action obvious.

11.why: Each screen asks for a single primary task (sign-in details or enter code) with one main button.

12.why: After failure only a generic banner appears; success/next-step feedback is not shown in the screenshots.

13.why: User can resubmit and choose “Use different details,” but no re-request/reveal-code action is offered.

14.why: Error only says “We could not complete that request. Please try again,” without naming the problem or fix.

15.why: No reading time limit is shown and the code’s 10-minute expiry is reasonably generous for entry.
